newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Tension rises in East Timor as arrests continue.
newsitem.headline: Tension rises in East Timor as arrests continue.

text.p: Tensions have risen in East Timor's capital of Dili as Indonesian security officers continue searching for local youths suspected of involvement in the killing of a soldier on Christmas Eve, residents said on Sunday.
"The youths have become more and more restless because of the continuing search at night," one resident told Reuters by telephone from Dili.
Residents said police and military officers had recently rounded up the youths at night for questioning.

East Timor Deputy Police Chief Lieutenant-Colonel Atok Rismanto said this week police had detained 15 people suspected of involvement in the killing of Corporal Alfredo dos Santos and pledged to arrest more.
Police were not available for comment on Sunday.
Residents said there were no reports of further incidents overnight and that masses in churches in the predominantly Catholic region proceeded smoothly on Sunday morning.

Dos Santos was beaten to death near Dili's cathedral on December 24. On the same day, several other police and soldiers were attacked by members of the crowd welcoming Nobel Peace Prize laureate Bishop Carlos Belo back to the territory.
The Indonesian military said the dead man, who was wearing civilian clothes, was off-duty and visiting the cathedral as a worshipper on his own accord.
Belo has publicly apologised for the death of the soldier, a native of East Timor and father of seven.

Indonesian troops invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in December 1975 and made it Indonesia's 27th province the following year. The move was not recognised by the United Nations, which regards Lisbon as the territory's administering power.
